narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate the historical improvement and progression of 100m freestyle swimming times across 116 years of Olympic history.

units.meaning: The clip presents one ordered historical series of relative values, not a set of separate unrelated categories.
accepted_routes: a single continuous series running from the opening point to the closing point
one ordered historical progression of relative values
a continuous line or path of values rather than independent bars
units.visual_evidence_rule: A single continuous series is visible across the ordered points, connecting the opening and closing values.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about gliding over Olympic history
units.reviewer_question: Must the video show one continuous ordered series, rather than separate unconnected points or categories?

units.meaning: The relative value trends downward overall from the opening point to the closing point.
accepted_routes: the series declines from 0.8934 at the opening to 0.0202 at the close
overall downward progression from near the top of the relative scale to near the bottom
the historical trend moves lower across the ordered points
units.visual_evidence_rule: The opening end of the series is visibly higher than the closing end, with an overall downward direction.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about gliding over Olympic history
units.reviewer_question: Must the overall downward direction from opening to closing be explicitly conveyed, not just individual values?

units.meaning: The opening point is the highest relative value in the series.
accepted_routes: the series starts at its maximum relative value, 0.8934
the highest point is the opening value
0.8934 is the top relative value shown
units.visual_evidence_rule: The first point is clearly the highest point in the series.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about swimming against every Olympic medalist
units.reviewer_question: Must the opening maximum of 0.8934 be shown or called out as the series high?

units.meaning: The closing point is the lowest relative value in the series.
accepted_routes: the series ends at its minimum relative value, 0.0202
the lowest point is the closing value
0.0202 is the bottom relative value shown
units.visual_evidence_rule: The final point is clearly the lowest point in the series.
units.reviewer_question: Must the closing minimum of 0.0202 be shown or called out as the series low?

units.meaning: The overall change from opening to closing is a drop of 0.8732 relative units, with the closing value about 1/44 of the opening value.
accepted_routes: the relative value falls by 0.8732 units from start to finish
the closing value is roughly one-fortieth of the opening value
most of the initial relative level is lost by the endpoint
units.visual_evidence_rule: The difference between the opening and closing values is visible or annotated.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about gliding over Olympic history
units.reviewer_question: Must the video quantify the overall drop, or is showing the downward direction sufficient?

optional_valid: The series is not monotonic: it contains local upward reversals (e.g., 0.1489 to 0.1801, and 0.0827 to 0.1232) before continuing downward.
The relative value crosses below half of the opening maximum between 0.4559 and 0.4430 (half of 0.8934 is 0.4467).
The series includes a labeled x_value of 1988 at one point in the progression.
unsupported_to_avoid: Any exact swimming time in seconds or minutes (not present in the table).
Any percentage improvement or percentage share (relative_value is a 0-1 normalization, not a percentage).
The long historical span as a numeric data value (not present in the table).
Causal explanations such as training, technology, or participation causing the change.
Swimmer names or medalist identities beyond the table rows.
Treating lower relative_value as an absolute time or as a proven causal measure of speed.
notes: The table is relative-only, so all units stay in ordering, direction, endpoint, and magnitude-of-relative-change terms. Values are normalized 0-1 scores, not percentages or absolute swimming times.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
